title: The Telegraph and Early Communication
text: The electric telegraph was the first system capable of nearly instantaneous long-distance communication. Samuel Morse, together with Alfred Vail, developed the first practical telegraph system in the United States in the 1830s and 1840s, also inventing Morse code — a system of dots and dashes representing letters and numbers. The first transatlantic telegraph cable was completed in 1858, linking North America and Europe. The telegraph transformed commerce, journalism, and military coordination, shrinking the effective communication distance between continents to near zero. It paved the way for all subsequent electronic communication technologies, from the telephone to the internet.
